## Web app

When using an AI in a web app (ChatGPT, Claude, etc.), you need to give it enough information to help you solve your problem.

This is easy to fix in theory, but in practice:

- we forget important details
- we ignore things that could be relevant
- we need to copy-paste lots of code
- we're lazy


## Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode, Pi...

- For over a year now, many developers have been using AI coding tools
- Those tools solve several problems you run into with web apps:

  - they have access to your whole project, not just what you give them
  - they decide what's relevant when answering your request (e.g., which files)
  - they can run shell commands (almost limitless possibilities)

## TUI

The default way to code with AI now is through a **Terminal User Interface** (TUI)

  - [where many devs already work]{.green}
  - [no browser limitations (e.g., file access)]{.green}
  - [faster]{.green}
  - [doesn't look as good]{.red}
